column1: # Counter-example: the same sweep as scaling/zip-sweep.tsv, run in a window
# whose pinned CPU set (17,21,22,25,28,29,30,31) turned out to contain three
# fully saturated CPUs belonging to other agents on this shared host. It is
# retained because it is the measured shape of a wave that has to wait for its
# workers to be scheduled: p50 values in whole milliseconds where the
# sequential leg is tens of microseconds, and A/A floors up to 118%.
# Nothing is claimed from these cells. They are the evidence behind the
# Limitations paragraph "on a saturated host the wave is a large loss".
# The corrected run, on CPUs measured idle immediately beforehand, is
# scaling/zip-sweep.tsv.
# Captured by probe/sweep.py with drive.py's CPU set fixed at
# "17,21,22,25,28,29,30,31", before the driver was changed to choose the
# quietest CPUs from /proc/stat at run time.
